name: wing-controller-design
notes: Machine-readable form of tokens.css, for an application or plugin that is not CSS.
This is the file a human edits: design/tokens.css is generated from it by scripts/generate-design-tokens.mjs, and
scripts/test-design-tokens-generator.mjs fails when the two disagree.
Light and dark are two complete sets. Do not invent a third.
Colours with meaning (accent, maroon, amber, green, yellow, red, gold) keep their meaning across apps; the greys are furniture.
The meter ramp is a foreign consumer's value (control-app session, openwing, 2026-10-07). Its key was renamed
meter-ramp -> meterRamp on 2026-10-08 so every key follows one convention; that rename is the kit's decision, and
the CSS property is still --meter-ramp.
The kit caught up with index.html on 2026-10-08 (ITEM 1): --dim is #4a4a4a light / #9aa8a2 dark (380122c7's measured
contrast audit) and --red is #b94444 (index.html's long-standing value from the 8be6a736 snapshot, not that audit).
meters.html still declares the kit's previous --dim and --red: the application's windows disagree with each other, so
that is a deviation to declare (ITEM 5), not a value the kit can copy from two windows at once.
The type scale gained four INSTRUMENT steps on 2026-10-08 (roadmap 4l, D-TYPE-4): the interface steps cap at 18px,
and the readings the operator actually watches are larger. Two jobs, two sizes each: `readout`/`readout-lg` are the
reported value inside a card or a panel (index.html's Timecode card and its Properties readout, 22/26px), and
`clock`/`clock-lg` are a window's clock face (ltc.html at 30px, and the cap of timecode.html's responsive clock at
52px). Their floors are the sizes measured in the windows, so naming them changed no pixel; the guide's 17px
chapter h2 stays a declared deviation, because a document hierarchy is not an instrument reading.
VERSION and this key went 1.0.1 -> 1.1.0 on 2026-10-08 with those four steps: adding tokens and changing the published
base (`--meter-scale` 1 -> 1.25, D-TYPE-5) is a MINOR, and a kit whose content changed under the same number is the
defect this kit exists to prevent - a consumer would take 1.0.1 believing it is what it was. Nothing was removed and
no existing name changed value, so a 1.0.1 consumer that re-copies is additive-safe except for the base.
VERSION and this key went 1.1.0 -> 1.2.0 on 2026-10-08 because the kit gained `design/components.css` - its component
layer. NO TOKEN CHANGED, and that is the point of the note: the version moved because the kit's CONTENT moved, and a
consumer that takes 1.2.0 receives a file it did not receive at 1.1.0. `tokens.json` is still the only file a human
edits; `components.css` is hand-written because a component is a drawing and not a value, and it is drawn entirely from
the tokens here. A 1.1.0 consumer that re-copies is additive-safe: same names, same values, one more file to link.

VERSION and this key went 1.2.0 -> 1.3.0 on 2026-10-08 because the DRAWINGS must address an element by what it IS by default, and `input:not([type])` joined the field list of `components.css`. A bare `<input>` is a text field by HTML, and a CSS attribute selector does not match an attribute that is absent, so the platform drew it: measured in this repository’s main window, where 42 bare inputs painted rgb(59, 59, 59) with white ink inside a LIGHT window under a dark-preferring browser. NO TOKEN CHANGED; the version moved because the kit’s content moved. A 1.2.0 consumer that re-copies is additive-safe: same names, same values, one selector wider.

TWO VALUES ARRIVED, AND ONE OF THEM IS A NEW KIND. `desk` (#008080 light, #0e1111 dark) is the ground the application's own window sits on: it is declared and used in this repository's main window (`desktop/ui/index.html:41`, `:4978`, `background: var(--desk)` at `:63` and `:81`) and was the one value a consumer of this kit had to spell outside it, so the kit names it now. `layout.opsColWidth` (420px, one value for both themes) is not a colour and not a size of type: it is the width of the operator column in the kit's composition layer (`design/layout.css`), and it is a token rather than a loose variable because `desktop/ui/index.html:172` writes it as `var(--ops-col-width, 420px)` through 32,000 lines that no consumer can find. `desk` is a colour the two themes disagree about; `opsColWidth` is the same in both, because the column is furniture and not a palette.

What the kit does NOT name, measured rather than omitted. `--desk-2` (#006868 light / #151918 dark) is declared beside `--desk` in the application's own `:root` (`index.html:42`, `:4979`) and is used by NOTHING in this repository (`grep -c 'var(--desk-2)' desktop/ui/*.html` is 0), so it is a dead declaration rather than a second desk step, and the kit does not give a dead value a name. `--surface` (#d4d0c8 / #1a1e1d) is the kit's `--face-2` under another name, and `--crt-2` is the second phosphor ground the windows carry; both stay where they are until a window can be migrated and the ten screenshots can be refreshed with it.

VERSION and this key went 1.3.0 -> 1.4.0 on 2026-10-08 because the kit gained `design/layout.css` and `design/layout.html` - its COMPOSITION layer - and two values above. The rules were not invented here: they are the four the application composes every window with (`desktop/ui/index.html`'s `.stack`, `.builder-column`, `.layout` and the `<main> -> header.master-header -> .layout -> .stack` chain), named and documented so that a consumer links the plan instead of copying four rules and guessing the rest - the same move that turned the button into `components.css`. A 1.3.0 consumer that re-copies is additive-safe: no name was removed, no existing value changed, and the two new names are two it may declare.

VERSION and this key went 1.4.0 -> 1.4.1 on 2026-10-08, and it is a PATCH with NO TOKEN CHANGED because the move repairs a number rather than publishes a value: the kit's CONTENT changed under 1.4.0 and the number did not, which is the exact defect every note above exists to prevent. `design/components.css` gained the window furniture (`89c27b47`) and the heading reset (`f869c8f0`) while `VERSION` still read 1.4.0, and this change adds to the artefact the three things its own documents already sent a consumer to and it did not carry: the reference window (`design/reference-window/index.html` with the region map in its `PLAN.md`), the `specimen.html` that the four `reference/` images are pictures of, and the suite's own proof (`conformance/self-test.mjs` with `conformance/fixtures/`). It also corrects `design/conformance/README.md`, whose title called the suite 'the eight acceptance points' and whose rule table listed eight of its rules, and the two adopt instructions that placed the kit's sheets where the suite does not read them. A consumer that re-copies 1.4.0 is additive-safe: no token name was removed, no token value changed, and it receives files and corrected sentences it did not receive before.

The kit gained ONE leading step on 2026-10-08: `leading.base` = 1.35, the line box of the page frame (`--leading-base`). The family is one step and not a scale because the measurement says the kit's drawings use one: neither `design/components.css` nor `design/layout.css` gave a control, card or panel a `line-height` (the one `layout.css` carries is section 0's `body` rule, added by this same change), so every drawing the kit ships inherits exactly one line box, and the two pages that compose a frame wrote the same value by hand (`design/layout.html:25`, `design/reference-window/index.html:26`). The value is the application's own rather than chosen here: `desktop/ui/index.html:88` sets `line-height: 1.35` on `body`, and it is the same 1.35 the two pages carried. Both pages now link `design/layout.css` and write none of it, and the rule they used to write by hand is that sheet's section 0, because `body` is the page's frame and not a drawing. `design/specimen.html` is not one of the two: it is a document page and not a window frame, it does not link `layout.css`, and it keeps its own 1.4 — naming 1.4 as a second step would invent a scale for one page, and replacing it with this step would re-render a page whose four photographs are `design/reference/`.

The family is spelled `leading` and not `line` on purpose: `--line`, `--line-mid`, `--line-light` and `--line-dark` are the bevel's four edge steps, and `design/conformance/rules.mjs`'s `tokenRole()` classifies any name matching /line/ as an edge colour, so a `--line-base` would read as a fifth bevel step. The step is named `base`, the kit's own word for the interface's base size (`--font-base`). The native form carries no member for it: `WingTheme.swift` carries the palette, the type scale, the spacing grid and the knob, and `layout.opsColWidth` has none there either (`design/README.md` point 10), so a line-height that is a CSS page-frame value stays in the CSS form.

**VERSION AND `design/package/**` ARE NOW OWED, and this note is their record.** This change adds content to the kit - a token, a rule in `layout.css`, a sample in `specimen.html` - without moving `design/VERSION` (still 1.4.1) and without regenerating the artefact, because the kit's owner has to move the version and the artefact together as one decision, and that decision is not this change's. The cost is measured rather than hidden: `scripts/test-design-kit-package.mjs` is red until the two move together, because the artefact's copies of the edited sources are stale by exactly these edits. `design/reference/specimen-type-and-space-both-themes.png` is owed a re-cut for the same reason (the specimen's own page grew by the new sample, so the last band of `design/reference/` no longer reaches the foot of it), and it was deliberately not re-cut here.

VERSION and this key went 1.4.1 -> 1.4.2 on 2026-10-08, and it is a PATCH with NO TOKEN VALUE CHANGED that pays the debt the note above records: `design/package/**` is regenerated and the artefact is cut again, in ONE commit whose message names every change it carries, because a message that names one thing while carrying eight is the defect this kit records everywhere. NO TOKEN NAME WAS REMOVED AND NO EXISTING VALUE CHANGED, so a 1.4.1 consumer that re-copies is additive-safe. What the regenerated artefact carries that 1.4.1's did not: the reference window's R4 arriving OPEN, with the fold moved onto the button and the theme label beside it, in `reference-window/index.html` and its `PLAN.md` (`09a2ffcc`); `layout.css` saying which shell it assumes and its own header bullet for the same question (`24c7bcdd`, `804dd1d4`); the kit's `card-head-row`, named where the card's head lives, in `components.css` (`52b76abf`); the `leading.base` step above and the `body` frame `layout.css` was missing (`f49878d5`); RULE 11 - a page must fit the window the suite renders in - with `conformance/fixtures/bad-overflow.html`, and the collector waiting for the page's own animations before it samples (`42bfde37`, `193b45ca`); the four `design/reference/` bands re-cut for the meter, the head row and the leading sample (`d7ceedf0`); the gate template `adopt/gate.sh.example`, which the artefact did not carry while two of its own documents told a consumer to run it (`4c2132dd`); and, by D11, a RUNNABLE `conformance/allow.mjs` composed at pack time from this VERSION - the declaration `conformance/run.mjs` reads by default, declaring the kit's own reference window with `deviations: []`, because the tarball shipped the example and not the file the judge reads, so a consumer's first documented command exited 3 with 'the app allowance file does not exist' and measured nothing. The prose corrections that travel with it are inside too: the checksum beside the tarball in `CONSUMING.md`, the theme snippet and the doubled semicolon in `UI_SYSTEM.md`, the package-versus-tarball step in `adopt/README.md`, the runnable gate in `adopt/wire-your-gate.md`, and the default declaration in `conformance/README.md`. The exemplar `adopt/allow.mjs.example` now spells 1.4.2.

type.winFont: "MS Sans Serif", "Microsoft Sans Serif", Tahoma, "Segoe UI", Geneva, sans-serif

bevel.raised: border-top/left: 1px solid var(--line-light); border-bottom/right: 1px solid var(--line-dark)
bevel.sunken: border-top/left: 1px solid var(--line-dark); border-bottom/right: 1px solid var(--line-light)
bevel.rule: A control is raised and a well is sunken. Never both on one element, and never a raised control without the light-before-dark pair. The pair is ONE step: the second inner step this application's own controls draw (`desktop/ui/index.html:1305-1318`, the light `--face-3` over the dark `--line-mid`) is a declared deviation of that window (`design/conformance/allow.mjs`, rule 1 `two-shapes`), not a second bevel the kit names — see `design/adopt/README.md` step 6 for the measurement and the reason the drawing was left alone.
